_about: Questions used only by the offline experiments, which score Jev's answers against labelled alerts in files.
The live receiver does not ask any of these; its questions are in alert_triage/questions.json.
Each one backs a measured decision; reword one and rerun its experiment to test that decision again.
Point ALERT_TRIAGE_EXPERIMENT_QUESTIONS at another file to keep several versions.
{n} is replaced by the two-digit number of the alert or group asked about.

same_event_as_any_recent_alert._used_by: triage.py score: the context experiment on the 300 simulated alerts
same_event_as_any_recent_alert._result: measured alongside urgency; never shown on the page
same_event_as_any_recent_alert.question: Does `alert` have the same underlying cause as at least one alert in `recent_alerts`?
same_event_as_any_recent_alert.yes: It shares a cause with a recent alert: the same fault or the same rollout, or one is an upstream or downstream symptom of the other
same_event_as_any_recent_alert.no: Every recent alert is unrelated to it: different services with no dependency between them, and no shared cause

same_cause_as_alert._used_by: incidents.py: splitting one Alertmanager group into separate problems
same_cause_as_alert._result: made precision and recall both worse, so splits are off
same_cause_as_alert.question: Does `alert` have the same underlying cause as `recent_alerts.alert_{n}`?
same_cause_as_alert.yes: One fault explains both: the same failure or the same rollout, or one is an upstream or downstream symptom of the other
same_cause_as_alert.no: Separate causes: each would have fired without the other, including two unrelated problems on the same service

same_cause_as_group._used_by: incidents.py: merging groups that share a cause (also tested on ITBench-Lite)
same_cause_as_group._result: a small gain on simulated alerts, little on ITBench-Lite, so merging was removed from the receiver
same_cause_as_group.question: Do the alerts in `group` have the same underlying cause as the alerts in `other_groups.group_{n}`? Each group is one Alertmanager notification group.
same_cause_as_group.yes: One fault explains both groups: the same failure or the same rollout, or one group's alerts are an upstream or downstream symptom of the other's
same_cause_as_group.no: Separate causes: each group would have fired without the other
